stemMd: A charity says its campaign succeeded because donations rose. When asked why donations rose, it answers that the campaign succeeded. As a justification, this reasoning

options.label: A
options.textMd: uses an analogy between unrelated charities.

options.label: B
options.textMd: offers the conclusion again as its own explanation without independent support.

options.label: C
options.textMd: draws an inference from a random sample.

options.label: D
options.textMd: confuses a necessary condition with a sufficient one.

explanationMd: Each statement is supported only by the other. Independent evidence—such as a comparison group or documented campaign-induced donations—is needed to establish why donations rose rather than relabeling the rise as success.

distractorRationale.d: The central issue is the circular explanation.
distractorRationale.e: Donation type is not relevant to the circularity.
